verses.text: The wife of a man from the company of prophets cried out to Elisha, “My husband, your servant, is dead. You know he honored the LORD. Now the man he owed money to has come to take my two children as slaves.”
Elisha asked her, “What can I do for you? Tell me what you have in the house.” She answered, “Nothing except a jar of oil.”
He said, “Go borrow empty containers from all your neighbors. Get as many as you can.
Then go inside with your sons and shut the door. Pour oil into all those containers and set each one aside as it fills.”
She left him and shut herself and her sons inside. They brought her the containers, and she poured the oil.
When all the containers were full, she told her son, “Bring me another one.” He said, “There isn't another one.” Then the oil stopped flowing.
She went and told the man of God. He said, “Go sell the oil, pay your debt, and live on what's left, you and your sons.”
One day Elisha went to Shunem. A prominent woman there urged him to stay for a meal. After that, whenever he passed through, he stopped there to eat.
She told her husband, “I can see that this man who keeps coming by is a holy man of God.
Let's make a little room for him on the roof, with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand. Then he can stay here whenever he comes.”
One day Elisha came and went up to the room to lie down.
He told his servant Gehazi, “Call the woman from Shunem.” Gehazi called her, and she came and stood before him.

Elisha told Gehazi, “Say to her, ‘You've gone to a lot of trouble for us. What can we do for you? Would you like me to speak on your behalf to the king or the army commander?’” She answered, “I live among my own people.”
Elisha asked, “What can we do for her, then?” Gehazi replied, “She has no son, and her husband is old.”
“Call her,” Elisha said. Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.
Elisha told her, “About this time next year you'll hold a son in your arms.” She said, “No, my lord, man of God. Please don't lie to me.”
But the woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son at that time the next year, just as Elisha had told her.
The boy grew, and one day he went out to his father, who was with the harvesters.
He cried to his father, “My head! My head!” His father told a servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
The servant carried him to his mother. The boy sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
She carried him upstairs, laid him on the man of God's bed, shut the door behind her, and went out.
She called to her husband, “Please send me one of the servants and a donkey so I can hurry to the man of God and come right back.”
“Why are you going today?” he asked. “It isn't the new moon or the Sabbath.” She answered, “It's all right.”
She saddled a donkey and told her servant, “Keep going. Don't slow down for me unless I tell you.”
So she went to see the man of God at Mount Carmel. He saw her coming from a distance and told his servant Gehazi, “Look, it's the woman from Shunem.
Run to meet her and ask, ‘Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is your child all right?’” She answered, “It's all right.”

When she reached the man of God on the mountain, she grabbed his feet. Gehazi came over to push her away, but the man of God told him, “Leave her alone. She's heartbroken, and the LORD has kept it from me. He hasn't told me what happened.”
Then she said, “Did I ask you for a son, my lord? Didn't I tell you, ‘Don't deceive me’?”
Elisha told Gehazi, “Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my staff, and go. Don't stop to greet anyone you meet, and don't answer anyone who greets you. Lay my staff on the boy's face.”
But the boy's mother said, “As surely as the LORD lives and as surely as you live, I won't leave you.” So Elisha got up and followed her.
Gehazi went on ahead and put the staff on the child's face. There was no sound or response. He went back to meet Elisha and told him, “The boy hasn't woken up.”
When Elisha got to the house, he saw the boy lying dead on his bed.
He went inside, shut the door so they were alone, and prayed to the LORD.
Then he climbed onto the bed and lay over the boy, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, and hands to hands. As he stretched himself over him, the boy's body grew warm.
Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room once. Then he climbed back up and stretched himself over the boy again. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
Elisha called Gehazi and said, “Call the woman from Shunem.” He called her, and when she came in, Elisha said, “Pick up your son.”
She came in and fell at his feet, bowing to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.
Elisha returned to Gilgal while there was a famine in the land. The company of prophets was sitting with him, and he told his servant, “Put the big pot on and make some stew for them.”
One of them went into the field to gather herbs. He found a wild vine and gathered a cloakful of wild gourds from it. He came back and sliced them into the pot of stew. Nobody knew what they were.
They served the stew to the men. As they began to eat, they cried out, “Man of God, there's death in the pot!” They couldn't eat it.
Elisha said, “Bring me some flour.” He threw it into the pot and said, “Serve it to the people so they can eat.” There was nothing harmful in the pot anymore.
A man from Baal Shalishah brought the man of God some bread from the first harvest, twenty barley loaves, and fresh heads of grain in his sack. Elisha said, “Give it to the people to eat.”
His servant asked, “How can I put this in front of a hundred people?” Elisha said, “Give it to them to eat. This is what the LORD says: ‘They'll eat and have some left over.’”
So he served them. They ate and had some left over, just as the LORD had said.
